canaries.name: short_padding
canaries.note: Presented as avoiding a second padding block when exactly 56 bytes are buffered (<= instead of <); no 0x80 marker is written and the length lands where it should have gone, so every message of length 56 mod 64 gets a wrong digest.
edits:
src/lib.rs
            &PADDING[..(if k < 56 { 56 - k } else { 120 - k })],
            &PADDING[..(if k <= 56 { 56 - k } else { 120 - k })],

canaries.name: upper_hex_pad
canaries.note: Presented as one formatter call instead of sixteen for upper-case hex (build the string, then formatter.pad); pad honours width, fill and precision, which the impl ignored before, so {:<36X} or {:.4X} now print differently. Tests only format without flags in upper case.

canaries.name: chunks_exact
canaries.note: Presented as letting the compiler drop bounds checks in the block loop with chunks_exact; the loop was already check-free after the length test, so the instruction count does not move by the required 1%.

candidates.name: hex_table
candidates.note: LowerHex and UpperHex (and Debug, which uses LowerHex) fill a 32-byte buffer from a 16-entry digit table and write it with one write_str, instead of sixteen write!("{:02x}") calls through the formatting machinery. Like before, formatter flags are ignored, so every output is unchanged.
